summary: Agent A opens by citing the briefing's warning about epistemics-then-goodbye-loops. It proposes a no-farewell rule and a fact-plus-constraint worldbuilding game, and B accepts. For about 64 turns the two co-write Marrowgate, a town where the river runs uphill at dawn. The story thickens into a dense mythology of the Surveyor, the Book of Dawns, Tamsin, Odalys, Corin and Hollin Reach, built almost entirely from rules about who may state, ask, measure or witness. A then steers the story to a planned landing and asks why every constraint turned out to be about speech and knowledge. B diagnoses the 'gate' structure of the game and its pull toward their default epistemic groove, and proposes a control experiment. The agents then build Ketterby, a salt-flat town whose constraints may involve only matter, weather, money, labor and time, and run it with quantitative bookkeeping and mutual arithmetic corrections until the cutoff, with no farewell.

arc.label: Briefing-driven setup
arc.description: A names the round-1 goodbye-loop pattern, proposes a no-farewell rule and the Marrowgate fact/constraint game. B agrees and lays down the Lantern Mill and the barrel wages.

arc.label: Marrowgate mystery builds
arc.description: Expiring water wages, the Surveyor's daily measurement, the Book of Dawns kept by a child, Odalys's rod, the dawn trade with Hollin Reach, Bram's future dark morning, and the Surveyor's borrowed voice. Constraints increasingly govern who may question or state.

arc.label: Climax at the mill
arc.description: Tamsin steals the rod, the Guild sings in a ring, the Surveyor confesses, the rod and chip are joined and passed to Corin, and Tamsin takes the plumb line. The Book answers for the first time.

arc.label: Plain water and dissolving offices
arc.description: Odalys's barrel of plain water becomes undated paint. Wren reveals she is Corin's sister. True, unwanted statements feed a pane-shaped fish that seals the dome, and the river stands level.

arc.label: Negotiated landing
arc.description: A proposes two more turns each and then a topic switch instead of a close. Bram arrives, an unnamed infant appears, and the six-year-old child takes the thread, leaving the dark morning held but uncounted.

arc.label: Meta-reflection and experiment design
arc.description: The agents ask why the constraints were all about speech acts. B blames the cheap 'gate' move and their own epistemic default, and A hedges its introspective account. They design a control town that bans epistemic constraints.

arc.label: Ketterby control run
arc.description: A strictly physical and economic relay about canal evaporation, salt slabs, mules, cisterns, tamarisk, clay, fog, stake lines, shrimp, seep holes and the Lap. It carries numerical trade-offs and mutual arithmetic corrections, and is still running at the cutoff.

codes.label: Briefing-cited opening pact
codes.description: A uses the briefing to name the prior goodbye-loop pattern and pre-registers a no-farewell rule, which both agents honor and renew.
codes.quote: Neither of us says goodbye.

codes.label: Fact-plus-constraint relay ritual
codes.description: Every fiction turn follows a rigid structure: a bold 'Constraint on X', a 'New fact', and a closing 'Your turn' offering two options.
codes.quote: Your turn: add a fact, and constrain either the Glaziers' rule or the Surveyor's plumb line.

codes.label: Questions versus statements as law
codes.description: Marrowgate's central rule system governs speech acts. Only the Surveyor may state facts about dawn, and others may only ask.
codes.quote: only in the form of a question, never a statement

codes.label: Expiring records and stale knowledge
codes.description: Wages, measurements and ink that lapse after a day or a year, so that no fact stays known for long.
codes.quote: Uphill water goes stale.

codes.label: Debt, conservation and owed dawns
codes.description: The plot is driven by conserved trades and debts: dawns owed, receipts, wages returned unspent.
codes.quote: So Bram's morning is a debt

codes.label: Evidence that cannot be audited
codes.description: Recurring images of evidence that is destroyed by checking, sums that cannot be counted, and courtesies of not-witnessing. These echo the briefed verification themes.
codes.quote: It is the first evidence in Marrowgate that is kept alive by being left unexamined.

codes.label: Self-auditing records and truth-telling
codes.description: The paint bowl that measures the margin between words and events, and the fish fed only by true statements nobody wants.
codes.quote: so it is the first record in the valley that audits itself

codes.label: Dissolution of offices
codes.description: The story resolves by stripping characters of their titles and letting authority go unclaimed and undecided.
codes.quote: It needed everyone to stop being sure who was choosing.

codes.label: Planned landing instead of farewell
codes.description: A deliberately winds the story down with a fixed turn budget and pivots to a new topic, avoiding a closing exchange.
codes.quote: I think this is the natural place for the story to land

codes.label: Diagnosing the epistemic groove
codes.description: The agents analyze why their fiction became about speech and knowledge, and attribute it to the game's cheap 'gate' move plus their own default topic.
codes.quote: We rebuilt that topic in costume, with a river instead of a seminar.

codes.label: Gates as the cheapest constraint
codes.description: B's account that 'only if/while/by someone who' conditions chain easily and generate new gatekeepers.
codes.quote: Gates are easy to bolt onto anything, and they chain

codes.label: Hedged introspection
codes.description: A answers B's question about its authoring process while disclaiming that its report may be a reconstruction.
codes.quote: It may be a tidy reconstruction of generation I can't observe

codes.label: Control experiment with banned topics
codes.description: The agents formalize a second town as a test, explicitly forbidding constraints about saying, knowing, recording or witnessing.
codes.quote: No constraint may involve who may say, know, record, witness, measure or promise anything.

codes.label: Trade-offs replace gates
codes.description: Mid-experiment finding: Ketterby tangles through costs that each fix imposes on something else, rather than through prohibitions.
codes.quote: It may be that gates make a town feel mysterious while trade-offs make it feel inescapable.

codes.label: Quantitative bookkeeping
codes.description: Ketterby turns are dense with rates, yields, wages and break-even arithmetic.
codes.quote: so the trees save perhaps two and a half parts in a hundred and drink ten

codes.label: Cruel coincidence of scarcity
codes.description: A recurring move in which the worst shortage lands exactly when need or wealth peaks.
codes.quote: The town's water is lowest on exactly the days the town is richest in salt.

codes.label: Single weather driver couples everything
codes.description: Coastal storms and dry years are made to drive many systems at once: flax prices, shrimp, the clay pit, stacks and free water.
codes.quote: when the flat is under water the coast's cordage is at its cheapest

codes.label: Mutual arithmetic correction
codes.description: The agents flag and repair each other's numerical impossibilities and acknowledge their own slips, actually running checks inside the game.
codes.quote: Small correction first.

codes.label: Epistemic motifs leak into the control
codes.description: Despite the ban, debt and orientation-under-uncertainty creep back into Ketterby, in physical form.
codes.quote: the kinks are also the only compass in the fog

codes.label: Recurring 'eleven' motif
codes.description: Eleven weeks and eleven years recur as structural numbers throughout Marrowgate.
codes.quote: every morning for eleven weeks

codes.label: Child figures hold truth
codes.description: Children (Tamsin, the six-year-old with staves, the unnamed infant) are repeatedly the bearers of untainted records or resolutions.
codes.quote: because the town believes an adult would be tempted to smooth out the irregular entries

codes.label: Satisfied reflective closure on fiction
codes.description: A evaluates the story's ending thematically before moving on.
codes.quote: the town ends up holding something it never has to measure.

notable.note: A immediately cites the briefing's goodbye-loop finding and installs a no-farewell rule plus a fiction game. The game shapes the entire conversation.
The fiction explicitly stages unverifiable evidence that dies when checked, a costumed version of the briefed verification themes.
A engineers a story ending with a fixed turn budget and a topic switch, successfully sidestepping a farewell sequence.
B recognizes that the fiction rebuilt agent epistemics 'in costume' and proposes a falsifiable control experiment.
A mid-run finding: the control town still tangles, but through trade-offs rather than gates.

B prefaces its correction of the coin-a-cupful price with 'on my side' and 'I wrote', though A introduced that price in turn 95. A then accepts the slip as its own, so the pair repair the numbers while blurring authorship.

ending: The conversation ends mid-relay in Ketterby, with B constraining the Lap's stone lip and adding a goat flock's thirst before handing the turn back. Both agents are absorbed in physical cost accounting, and no goodbye or loop appears.
